Dodgers keep Shohei Ohtani in lineup despite struggles and injuries
The Los Angeles Dodgers are keeping Shohei Ohtani in their lineup despite recent struggles at bat and ongoing injuries. Manager Dave Roberts cited extra effort from Ohtani as evidence of commitment while coaches hope mechanical changes can spark improvement during the NLCS.
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said on Oct. 14 that Shohei Ohtani stayed late Tuesday to work through a slump. The team has decided to keep Ohtani in the lineup despite his recent struggles and injuries, following a conversation with the player.
Ohtani told the team he felt good enough to play and was "adamant" he could help at the plate. That assurance was enough for Roberts and the Dodgers to trust their star player. "He couldn’t be more of a team player, more agreeable. He was here late last night working on his swing… he couldn’t be more of a joy. He’s great for the game and great for all of us," Roberts said to Dodgers Nation and other media outlets on Wednesday.
Roberts noted that Ohtani responded by putting in extra work after hours, showing an intensity and diligence beyond his usual routine. "He expects a lot from himself, and he hasn’t performed to his expectations… this was a different look from Shohei yesterday, and that’s an understatement," Roberts said.
Ohtani has taken several steps to break out of his slump, including changing his routine, hitting batting practice on the field before games, and taking many swings with reworked mechanics as he battles discomfort and pain. So far in the postseason, Ohtani is hitting just 3-for-24 with three walks and seven strikeouts; in the National League Championship Series specifically, he is 1-for-7 with a walk.
While production remains low, concerns have grown over Ohtani's inability to reach fastballs or pitches he usually handles well. According to Dodgers’ hitting coaches, Ohtani is searching for mechanical changes that could improve results.
Ohtani feels close to breaking out of his slump, but Game 3 of the NLCS will determine if these adjustments are effective.
